To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endothelial cells in networks, but not in monolayers, display calcium oscillation in response to histamine stimulation and that the oscillation is attenuated in networks with higher cell density.
endothelial cells sense and respond to external chemical stimuli according to vascular architecture through collective calcium signaling.
the collective calcium signaling in endothelial networks is regulated by cellular architecture and that this signaling modulates the histamine-induced cell contractility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental mechanisms that underlie collective cellular behavior in vascular structures.
the mechanisms of collective calcium signaling and its functional implications in diverse endothelial cell architectures.
the role of cellular architecture in intercellular calcium signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the architecture of endothelial cell networks can regulate intercellular calcium signaling and cellular response to external stimuli, providing a mechanistically-based understanding of vascular function and dysfunction.
cellular architectures can regulate collective calcium signaling and contractile responses in a cell-type and stimulus-specific manner.
endothelial cells in vascular networks sense and respond to external stimuli in an architecture-dependent way, via collective calcium signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the architecture of vascular endothelial cells is an important determinant of collective cell signaling and function.
the cellular architecture is an important regulator of collective cellular responses to external stimuli.
endothelial cell architecture plays an essential role in collective calcium signaling, which regulates endothelial cell contractility in response to external chemical signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collective calcium signaling can regulate endothelial cell contractility and thus modulate vascular function.
the architecture of vascular networks regulates collective calcium signaling and the cell contractility, which is a key feature of multicellularity.
the architecture of the vasculature regulates the collective cell signaling that in turn regulates cell contractility and vascular function.
